text.p: These are the leading stories in the Kenyan press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Nairobi and Egerton universities are closed following demonstrations and skirmishes between police and students.
- Public outrage at the death of Nairobi student leader Solomon Muruli grows as leaders and members of the public blame the goverment and the police for his "murder".
- A British robbery and fraud expert arrives to investigate the theft of 96 million shillings at Standard Chartered Bank on Tuesday.
- An opposition member of parliament and a by-election candidate are injured when youths beat them up.
- A Kisumu court hears how a murder suspect was tied upside down on a tree while her police interrogators hit her on the knees and elbows in an effort to obtain a confession.
- A high court judge accuses the media of violating privacy rights of women and children involved in court cases especially in cases involving sexual harassment and rape.
- The remains of Lady Diana Delamere, widow of the late Lord Delamere, are dug up and golden ornaments worth millions of shillings are stolen from the coffin.
- George Nyanja, director of elections in the opposition FORD-Asili party, declares the party dead.
- The ministry of local government discloses Nairobi city council spends nearly 87 percent of its revenue on employee salaries. ($1=54 Kenyan shillings)
